NTE is surprisingly generous for a gacha. The system makes getting characters pretty painless. There’s no 50/50, an S-Class on the limited banner is guaranteed to be the featured character, soft pity kicks in at 70 pulls, hard pity is 90, and pity carries over.

At least starting out, there’s also a ton of content to play through that gives you enough Annulith and other rewards to potentially last you through a new banner or two without spending. The events also seem to give out a pretty good amount of currency, which is refreshing for a gacha that could easily be much more stingy.

It’s a really cool game with a fun world, characters, and gameplay. That said, once Ananta comes out, I could see it being hard for NTE to keep up, because that game looks like it could be crazy good.

Neverness to Everness really surprised me. Its biggest strength, in my opinion, is Hethereau, a beautiful city full of personality that genuinely makes you want to explore every corner of it. 🌆✨

The combat is fun, the characters have amazing designs, and being able to explore the city in different ways makes simply wandering around part of the experience.

It still has room for improvement, especially when it comes to performance and some of its systems, but its world, visual style, and overall personality give it a lot of potential.

If you enjoy action RPGs, open worlds, and stylish characters, NTE is definitely worth checking out. 🎮💜

So I've been playing a ton of gatcha games since Covid and this one is one of the most interesting ones I've had the pleasure of placing my hands on.

As for the gatcha system itself, it's better then most. Soft pity at 70, hard at 90. When pulling on a limited banner (one character exclusive) you get that character on pity. No-one else. 
Oh and it has a "skip" button for stories that offers a "recap" for important quests. For those who don't like listening to yap 
All in all, at my current hours would recommend

I have played NTE since the first global version on the standalone launcher. After some time, I decided to install it on Steam. It is truly a fun game. Mostly chill, except for some more difficult activities. The plot is fine, gameplay is mega smooth and polished, the gacha system is really fair - you don't have 50/50. However, it is balanced in a way - it is hard to get the character without "board modification", so usually 70+ pity is the moment you can anticipate her/him - although it is possible to drop the character earlier, of course. Speaking of characters - they are truly well made. Visuals, voice acting, animations, etc. - they are from the top shelf. Normal life in Hethereau as well as bond system is something fun as well - you can spend time with your favourite characters and enjoy yourself. Open world exploration is also really good - it is a pleasure, and I want to highlight this, because exploration in some games is such a pain in the neck. Comparing ToF (Tower of Fantasy) to NTE - Neverness to Everness does everything better. Furthermore, developers actually listen to players. So, the last thing I can do in this review is to simply wish Hotta Studio everything the best. I can't wait to see how the game will evolve, because it is one of the better gacha games available now (at least for me).

This game is a visual and gameplay marvel. It is extremely addicting. Way too many things to do in game, yet painfully slow progression. The engagement mechanics are devised to keep gamers hooked and logging it daily, but never fulfilling enough. New and desirable content is added frequently, but for a limited time, without ever really letting you catch up. Everyday I consider just spending money to get in game materials to speed up the progression and collect the obtainables. The progression without spending money is so tedious and grindy, and that is exactly what the game is designed to be. Welcome to gatcha.

In the end it is a gacha game with everything that comes with it... Not bad time, but still not really something I can recommend. 

Nothing is offensively bad. World is fine. Gameplay is mostly fine. Story well varies sometimes over dragged sometimes okay... Some parts of game are decent. Others really leave to hope for more. Sometimes with too many annoyances

But as said it is gacha, with absolutely everything that comes up with it. Too much effort for too little to gain. Too much busywork. Too expensive if you would pay... In the end it is still random gambling even if it is not the worst...
